title: Representing a graph
summary: Adjacency lists, directed vs undirected edges, degrees.
hints: Start with `g := make(Graph, n)`: that gives you `n` neighbour lists, one per vertex, each of them a nil slice. A nil slice is a perfectly good empty list, so `g[u] = append(g[u], v)` works straight away. An undirected edge also needs `g[v] = append(g[v], u)`.
`OutDegree` is just the length of one list: `len(g[u])`. `HasEdge` can loop over `g[u]` looking for `v`, or call `slices.Contains(g[u], v)` (import `"slices"`).

`InDegrees`: make a result `make([]int, len(g))` (all zeros), then walk every list of every vertex with `for _, neighbours := range g { for _, v := range neighbours { ... } }` and do `deg[v]++` for each neighbour found.
